chapters.summary: God creates the heavens and the earth in six days through his spoken word, ordering chaos into creation.
chapters.historical_note: Composed against ancient Near Eastern polytheistic creation myths. One sovereign God creates by speaking.
chapters.cultural_note: The seven-day week was distinctive to Hebrew culture. Each day is marked by the formula and there was evening and there was morning.

chapters.summary: God rests on the seventh day; the creation of man from dust and woman from man establishes the first covenant relationship.
chapters.historical_note: Genesis 2 uses an intimate narrative style focusing on the Garden of Eden near the Tigris and Euphrates.
chapters.cultural_note: Adam (adamah) means ground. The garden narrative establishes vocation, relationship, and the tension between obedience and autonomy.

verse_headings.heading_text: The Creation of the Heavens and the Earth
The Formation of Man and Woman

verses.english_text: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
verses.literal_text: In-beginning created God the-heavens and the-earth.
verses.original_text: בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.transliteration: Bereshit bara Elohim et hashamayim ve'et ha'arets.
verses.verse_note: The first word Bereshit establishes time itself as created. God precedes the beginning.
verses.historical_note: Composed against Mesopotamian polytheistic creation myths — radically monotheistic.
verses.cultural_note: Jewish tradition reads this on Rosh Hashanah as the origin point of time.
verses.language_note: Bara (Qal perfect) is used exclusively with God as subject throughout the OT.

verses.english_text: The earth was formless and empty, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.
verses.literal_text: And-the-earth was formless and-void, and-darkness over face-of the-deep; and-Spirit-of God hovering over face-of the-waters.
verses.original_text: וְהָאָרֶץ הָיְתָה תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ וְחֹשֶׁךְ עַל־פְּנֵי תְהוֹם וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים מְרַחֶפֶת עַל־פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם׃
verses.transliteration: Veha'arets hayetah tohu vavohu vechoshech al-peney tehom veruach Elohim merachefet al-peney hamayim.
verses.verse_note: Tohu vavohu is a Hebrew rhyming pair for utter formlessness — the raw state before God's ordering.
verses.cultural_note: Rachaph (hovering) is used of an eagle over her young (Deut 32:11) — watchful nurturing presence.

verses.english_text: And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.
verses.literal_text: And-said God, Let-be light, and-was light.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יְהִי אוֹר וַיְהִי־אוֹר׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer Elohim yehi or vayehi-or.
verses.verse_note: God creates by speaking. The divine speech act repeats 8 times in Genesis 1.
verses.language_note: Yehi is a jussive meaning let there be. The immediate response shows absolute divine authority.

verses.english_text: God saw that the light was good, and God separated the light from the darkness.
verses.literal_text: And-saw God the-light that good; and-separated God between the-light and-between the-darkness.
verses.original_text: וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הָאוֹר כִּי־טוֹב וַיַּבְדֵּל אֱלֹהִים בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ׃
verses.transliteration: Vayar Elohim et-ha'or ki-tov vayavdel Elohim beyn ha'or uveyn hachoshech.
verses.verse_note: Ki tov (it was good) appears 7 times in Gen 1 — its sevenfold recurrence mirrors the seven-day week.

verses.english_text: God called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night. And there was evening and there was morning, the first day.
verses.literal_text: And-called God to-the-light Day, and-to-the-darkness he-called Night. And-was evening and-was morning, day one.
verses.original_text: וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם וְלַחֹשֶׁךְ קָרָא לָיְלָה וַיְהִי־עֶרֶב וַיְהִי־בֹקֶר יוֹם אֶחָד׃
verses.transliteration: Vayikra Elohim la'or yom velachoshech kara laylah vayehi-erev vayehi-voker yom echad.
verses.language_note: Day one uses cardinal (yom echad) not ordinal — unique in the sequence; subsequent days use ordinals.

verses.english_text: And God said, "Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and let it separate the waters from the waters."
verses.literal_text: And-said God, Let-be expanse in-midst-of the-waters, and-let-it-separate between waters and-between waters.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יְהִי רָקִיעַ בְּתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם וִיהִי מַבְדִּיל בֵּין מַיִם לָמָיִם׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer Elohim yehi rakia betoch hamayim vihi mavdil beyn mayim lamayim.

verses.english_text: And God made the expanse and separated the waters that were under the expanse from the waters that were above the expanse. And it was so.
verses.literal_text: And-made God the-expanse and-separated between the-waters under the-expanse and-between the-waters above the-expanse. And-was so.
verses.original_text: וַיַּעַשׂ אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הָרָקִיעַ וַיַּבְדֵּל בֵּין הַמַּיִם אֲשֶׁר מִתַּחַת לָרָקִיעַ וּבֵין הַמַּיִם אֲשֶׁר מֵעַל לָרָקִיעַ וַיְהִי־כֵן׃
verses.transliteration: Vayaas Elohim et-harakia vayavdel beyn hamayim asher mitachat larakia uveyn hamayim asher me'al larakia vayehi-chen.

verses.english_text: And God called the expanse Heaven. And there was evening and there was morning, the second day.
verses.literal_text: And-called God to-the-expanse Heaven. And-was evening and-was morning, day second.
verses.original_text: וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָרָקִיעַ שָׁמָיִם וַיְהִי־עֶרֶב וַיְהִי־בֹקֶר יוֹם שֵׁנִי׃
verses.transliteration: Vayikra Elohim larakia shamayim vayehi-erev vayehi-voker yom sheni.

verses.english_text: And God said, "Let the waters under the heavens be gathered together into one place, and let the dry land appear." And it was so.
verses.literal_text: And-said God, Let-be-gathered the-waters under the-heavens to-one place and-let-appear the-dry-land. And-was so.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יִקָּווּ הַמַּיִם מִתַּחַת הַשָּׁמַיִם אֶל־מָקוֹם אֶחָד וְתֵרָאֶה הַיַּבָּשָׁה וַיְהִי־כֵן׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer Elohim yikavu hamayim mitachat hashamayim el-makom echad vetere'eh hayabashah vayehi-chen.

verses.english_text: God called the dry land Earth, and the waters that were gathered together He called Seas. And God saw that it was good.
verses.literal_text: And-called God to-the-dry-land Earth, and-to-the-gathering-of the-waters he-called Seas. And-saw God that good.
verses.original_text: וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לַיַּבָּשָׁה אֶרֶץ וּלְמִקְוֵה הַמַּיִם קָרָא יַמִּים וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי־טוֹב׃
verses.transliteration: Vayikra Elohim layabashah erets ulemikve hamayim kara yamim vayar Elohim ki-tov.

verses.english_text: And God said, "Let the earth sprout vegetation, plants yielding seed, and fruit trees bearing fruit in which is their seed, each according to its kind, on the earth." And it was so.
verses.literal_text: And-said God, Let-sprout the-earth vegetation: plants seeding seed and fruit-trees making fruit according-to-its-kind. And-was so.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים תַּדְשֵׁא הָאָרֶץ דֶּשֶׁא עֵשֶׂב מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע עֵץ פְּרִי עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי לְמִינוֹ אֲשֶׁר זַרְעוֹ־בוֹ עַל־הָאָרֶץ וַיְהִי־כֵן׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer Elohim tadsheh ha'arets deshe esev mazria zera ets peri oseh peri lemino asher zaro-vo al-ha'arets vayehi-chen.

verses.english_text: The earth brought forth vegetation, plants yielding seed according to their own kinds, and trees bearing fruit in which is their seed, each according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.literal_text: And-brought-forth the-earth vegetation: plants seeding seed according-to-its-kind and-trees making fruit which its-seed in-it according-to-its-kind. And-saw God that good.
verses.original_text: וַתּוֹצֵא הָאָרֶץ דֶּשֶׁא עֵשֶׂב מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע לְמִינֵהוּ וְעֵץ עֹשֶׂה־פְּרִי אֲשֶׁר זַרְעוֹ־בוֹ לְמִינֵהוּ וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי־טוֹב׃
verses.transliteration: Vatotse ha'arets deshe esev mazria zera leminehu ve'ets oseh-peri asher zaro-vo leminehu vayar Elohim ki-tov.

verses.english_text: And there was evening and there was morning, the third day.
verses.literal_text: And-was evening and-was morning, day third.
verses.original_text: וַיְהִי־עֶרֶב וַיְהִי־בֹקֶר יוֹם שְׁלִישִׁי׃
verses.transliteration: Vayehi-erev vayehi-voker yom shelishi.

verses.english_text: And God said, "Let there be lights in the expanse of the heavens to separate the day from the night. And let them be for signs and for seasons, and for days and years."
verses.literal_text: And-said God, Let-be luminaries in-expanse-of the-heavens to-separate between the-day and-between the-night; and-let-them-be for-signs and-for-seasons and-for-days and-years.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יְהִי מְאֹרֹת בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם לְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין הַיּוֹם וּבֵין הַלַּיְלָה וְהָיוּ לְאֹתֹת וּלְמוֹעֲדִים וּלְיָמִים וְשָׁנִים׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer Elohim yehi me'orot birakia hashamayim lehavdil beyn hayom uveyn halayla vehayu le'otot ulemo'adim uleyamim veshanim.
verses.verse_note: Luminaries created on day 4 — after light on day 1. This subordinates sun and moon to created status.
verses.cultural_note: Sun and moon never named here — a polemic against sun/moon worship in Egypt (Ra) and Mesopotamia.

verses.english_text: And let them be lights in the expanse of the heavens to give light upon the earth. And it was so.
verses.literal_text: And-let-them-be for-luminaries in-expanse-of the-heavens to-give-light upon the-earth. And-was so.
verses.original_text: וְהָיוּ לִמְאוֹרֹת בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם לְהָאִיר עַל־הָאָרֶץ וַיְהִי־כֵן׃
verses.transliteration: Vehayu limeorot birakia hashamayim leha'ir al-ha'arets vayehi-chen.

verses.english_text: And God made the two great lights — the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night — and the stars.
verses.literal_text: And-made God the-two great luminaries — the-great luminary for-dominion-of the-day and-the-small luminary for-dominion-of the-night — and the-stars.
verses.original_text: וַיַּעַשׂ אֱלֹהִים אֶת־שְׁנֵי הַמְּאֹרֹת הַגְּדֹלִים אֶת הַמָּאוֹר הַגָּדֹל לְמֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַיּוֹם וְאֶת הַמָּאוֹר הַקָּטֹן לְמֶמְשֶׁלֶת הַלַּיְלָה וְאֵת הַכּוֹכָבִים׃
verses.transliteration: Vayaas Elohim et-shnei hame'orot hagdolim et hama'or hagadol lememshelet hayom ve'et hama'or hakaton lememshelet halayla ve'et hakochavim.
verses.language_note: Sun and moon unnamed — polemic against their deification in Egypt (Ra) and Mesopotamia.

verses.english_text: And God set them in the expanse of the heavens to give light on the earth,
verses.literal_text: And-gave God them in-expanse-of the-heavens to-give-light upon the-earth,
verses.original_text: וַיִּתֵּן אֹתָם אֱלֹהִים בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם לְהָאִיר עַל־הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.transliteration: Vayiten otam Elohim birakia hashamayim leha'ir al-ha'arets,

verses.english_text: to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
verses.literal_text: to-rule in-the-day and-in-the-night and-to-separate between the-light and-between the-darkness. And-saw God that good.
verses.original_text: וְלִמְשֹׁל בַּיּוֹם וּבַלַּיְלָה וּלְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין הָאוֹר וּבֵין הַחֹשֶׁךְ וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי־טוֹב׃
verses.transliteration: Velimshol bayom uvalayla ulehavdil beyn ha'or uveyn hachoshech vayar Elohim ki-tov.

verses.english_text: And there was evening and there was morning, the fourth day.
verses.literal_text: And-was evening and-was morning, day fourth.
verses.original_text: וַיְהִי־עֶרֶב וַיְהִי־בֹקֶר יוֹם רְבִיעִי׃
verses.transliteration: Vayehi-erev vayehi-voker yom revi'i.

verses.english_text: And God said, "Let the waters swarm with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the expanse of the heavens."
verses.literal_text: And-said God, Let-swarm the-waters swarms of living-souls, and-birds let-fly above the-earth across face-of expanse-of the-heavens.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים יִשְׁרְצוּ הַמַּיִם שֶׁרֶץ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה וְעוֹף יְעוֹפֵף עַל־הָאָרֶץ עַל־פְּנֵי רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer Elohim yishretu hamayim sherets nefesh chaya ve'of ye'ofef al-ha'arets al-peney rakia hashamayim.

verses.english_text: So God created the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters swarm, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.literal_text: And-created God the-great sea-creatures and-all living-soul the-moving according-to-their-kind and-all winged-bird according-to-its-kind. And-saw God that good.
verses.original_text: וַיִּבְרָא אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הַתַּנִּינִם הַגְּדֹלִים וְאֵת כָּל נֶפֶשׁ הַחַיָּה הָרֹמֶשֶׂת אֲשֶׁר שָׁרְצוּ הַמַּיִם לְמִינֵהֶם וְאֵת כָּל עוֹף כָּנָף לְמִינֵהוּ וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי־טוֹב׃
verses.transliteration: Vayivra Elohim et-hataninim hagdolim ve'et kol nefesh hachaya haromesets asher shatsu hamayim leminehem ve'et kol of kanaf leminehu vayar Elohim ki-tov.
verses.verse_note: Taninim (sea creatures) are the same word as mythological sea monsters in Canaanite religion — here demythologised as created beings.

verses.english_text: And God blessed them, saying, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth."
verses.literal_text: And-blessed them God saying, Be-fruitful and-multiply and-fill the-waters in-the-seas, and-the-birds let-multiply on-the-earth.
verses.original_text: וַיְבָרֶךְ אֹתָם אֱלֹהִים לֵאמֹר פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ וּמִלְאוּ אֶת־הַמַּיִם בַּיַּמִּים וְהָעוֹף יִרֶב בָּאָרֶץ׃
verses.transliteration: Vayevarech otam Elohim lemor peru urvu umil'u et-hamayim bayamim vehe'of yirev ba'arets.

verses.english_text: And there was evening and there was morning, the fifth day.
verses.literal_text: And-was evening and-was morning, day fifth.
verses.original_text: וַיְהִי־עֶרֶב וַיְהִי־בֹקֶר יוֹם חֲמִישִׁי׃
verses.transliteration: Vayehi-erev vayehi-voker yom chamishi.

verses.english_text: And God said, "Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds — livestock and creeping things and beasts of the earth according to their kinds." And it was so.
verses.literal_text: And-said God, Let-bring-forth the-earth living-soul according-to-its-kind: livestock and-creeping-thing and-beast-of earth according-to-its-kind. And-was so.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים תּוֹצֵא הָאָרֶץ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה לְמִינָהּ בְּהֵמָה וָרֶמֶשׂ וְחַיְתוֹ אֶרֶץ לְמִינָהּ וַיְהִי־כֵן׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer Elohim totse ha'arets nefesh chaya leminah behema varemes vechaito erets leminah vayehi-chen.

verses.english_text: And God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds and the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that creeps on the ground according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
verses.literal_text: And-made God beast-of the-earth according-to-its-kind and-the-livestock according-to-its-kind and-all creeping-thing-of the-ground according-to-its-kind. And-saw God that good.
verses.original_text: וַיַּעַשׂ אֱלֹהִים אֶת חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ לְמִינָהּ וְאֶת הַבְּהֵמָה לְמִינָהּ וְאֵת כָּל רֶמֶשׂ הָאֲדָמָה לְמִינֵהוּ וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי־טוֹב׃
verses.transliteration: Vayaas Elohim et chayyat ha'arets leminah ve'et habehema leminah ve'et kol remes ha'adama leminehu vayar Elohim ki-tov.

verses.english_text: Then God said, "Let us make mankind in our image, according to our likeness, and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the livestock, all the earth, and all the creatures that move along the ground."
verses.literal_text: And-said God, Let-us-make man in-our-image, according-to-our-likeness, and-let-them-have-dominion over fish-of the-sea and-over birds-of the-heavens and-over the-livestock and-over all the-earth.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים נַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בְּצַלְמֵנוּ כִּדְמוּתֵנוּ וְיִרְדּוּ בִדְגַת הַיָּם וּבְעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וּבַבְּהֵמָה וּבְכָל־הָאָרֶץ וּבְכָל הָרֶמֶשׂ הָרֹמֵשׂ עַל הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer Elohim naase adam betsalmenu kidmutenu veyirdu bidgat hayam uveoph hashamayim uvavehema uvechol-ha'arets uvechol haremes haromes al ha'arets.
verses.verse_note: The plural let us make has generated theological debate: divine council, plural of deliberation, or Trinitarian plurality.
verses.cultural_note: Tselem Elohim (image of God) was used of royal statues in the ancient Near East — here democratised to all humanity.

verses.english_text: So God created mankind in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
verses.literal_text: And-created God the-man in-his-image, in-image-of God he-created him, male and-female he-created them.
verses.original_text: וַיִּבְרָא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם בְּצַלְמוֹ בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים בָּרָא אֹתוֹ זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה בָּרָא אֹתָם׃
verses.transliteration: Vayivra Elohim et ha'adam betsalmo betselem Elohim bara oto zachar uneqevah bara otam.
verses.verse_note: Threefold repetition of bara and explicit mention of male and female give this verse rhythmic emphasis. Image-bearing applies equally to both genders.

verses.english_text: And God blessed them. And God said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it, and have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing that moves on the earth."
verses.literal_text: And-blessed them God, and-said to-them God, Be-fruitful and-multiply and-fill the-earth and-subdue-it; and-have-dominion over fish-of the-sea and-over bird-of the-heavens and-over all living-thing the-moving upon the-earth.
verses.original_text: וַיְבָרֶךְ אֹתָם אֱלֹהִים וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם אֱלֹהִים פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ וּמִלְאוּ אֶת הָאָרֶץ וְכִבְשֻׁהָ וּרְדוּ בִּדְגַת הַיָּם וּבְעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וּבְכָל חַיָּה הָרֹמֶשֶׂת עַל הָאָרֶץ׃
verses.transliteration: Vayevarech otam Elohim vayomer lahem Elohim peru urvu umil'u et ha'arets vechivshuha urdu bidgat hayam uve'of hashamayim uvechol chaya haromesets al ha'arets.

verses.english_text: And God said, "Behold, I have given you every plant yielding seed that is on the face of all the earth, and every tree with seed in its fruit. You shall have them for food."
verses.literal_text: And-said God, See, I-have-given to-you every plant seeding seed which on face-of all the-earth, and-every tree which in-it fruit-of a-tree seeding seed; to-you it-shall-be for-food.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים הִנֵּה נָתַתִּי לָכֶם אֶת כָּל עֵשֶׂב זֹרֵעַ זֶרַע אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי כָל הָאָרֶץ וְאֶת כָּל הָעֵץ אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ פְרִי עֵץ זֹרֵעַ זָרַע לָכֶם יִהְיֶה לְאָכְלָה׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer Elohim hineh natati lachem et kol esev zorea zera asher al peney chol ha'arets ve'et kol ha'ets asher bo peri ets zorea zara lachem yihyeh le'ochlah.

verses.english_text: And to every beast of the earth and to every bird of the heavens and to everything that creeps on the earth, everything that has the breath of life, I have given every green plant for food. And it was so.
verses.literal_text: And-to-every beast-of the-earth and-to-every bird-of the-heavens and-to-everything creeping upon the-earth which in-it living-soul, every green plant for-food. And-was so.
verses.original_text: וּלְכָל חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ וּלְכָל עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וּלְכֹל רוֹמֵשׂ עַל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה אֶת כָּל יֶרֶק עֵשֶׂב לְאָכְלָה וַיְהִי כֵן׃
verses.transliteration: Ulechol chayyat ha'arets ulechol of hashamayim ulechol romes al ha'arets asher bo nefesh chaya et kol yerech esev le'ochlah vayehi chen.

verses.english_text: And God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.
verses.literal_text: And-saw God all that he-made, and-behold very good. And-was evening and-was morning, day the-sixth.
verses.original_text: וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר יוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי׃
verses.transliteration: Vayar Elohim et kol asher asah vehineh tov me'od vayehi erev vayehi voker yom hashishi.
verses.verse_note: The evaluation changes to very good (tov me'od) at the completion of all creation including mankind — the pinnacle.

verses.english_text: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.
verses.literal_text: And-were-finished the-heavens and-the-earth and-all their-host.
verses.original_text: וַיְכֻלּוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ וְכָל צְבָאָם׃
verses.transliteration: Vayechulu hashamayim veha'arets vechol tseva'am.
verses.verse_note: Vayechulu shares a root with Shabbat. Host (tsava) refers to the entire created order — stars, creatures, everything.

verses.english_text: And on the seventh day God finished His work that He had done, and He rested on the seventh day from all His work that He had done.
verses.literal_text: And-finished God on-the-day the-seventh his-work which he-did; and-rested on-the-day the-seventh from-all his-work which he-did.
verses.original_text: וַיְכַל אֱלֹהִים בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וַיִּשְׁבֹּת בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה׃
verses.transliteration: Vayechal Elohim bayom hashevi'i melachto asher asah vayishbot bayom hashevi'i mikol melachto asher asah.
verses.language_note: Vayishbot — he rested — is the root of Shabbat. God's rest is completion, a cessation that hallows the seventh day.

verses.english_text: So God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it God rested from all His work that He had done in creation.
verses.literal_text: And-blessed God the-day the-seventh and-sanctified it, because on-it he-rested from-all his-work which God created to-do.
verses.original_text: וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ כִּי בוֹ שָׁבַת מִכָּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים לַעֲשׂוֹת׃
verses.transliteration: Vayevarech Elohim et yom hashevi'i vayekadesh oto ki vo shavat mikol melachto asher bara Elohim la'asot.
verses.verse_note: The first use of holy (kadosh) in Scripture — associated first with time, not a place or person.
verses.historical_note: The Sabbath becomes the cornerstone of Israelite worship rhythm and the basis for the fourth commandment.

verses.english_text: These are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made the earth and the heavens.
verses.literal_text: These are the generations-of the-heavens and-the-earth in-their-being-created, in-the-day made the-LORD God earth and-heavens.
verses.original_text: אֵלֶּה תוֹלְדוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ בְּהִבָּרְאָם בְּיוֹם עֲשׂוֹת יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם׃
verses.transliteration: Eleh toledot hashamayim veha'arets behivar'am beyom asot YHWH Elohim erets veshamayim.
verses.verse_note: Hinge verse between the cosmic account (1:1-2:3) and the intimate garden narrative. Introduces YHWH for the first time.
verses.language_note: Toledot (generations) is a structural formula used throughout Genesis to begin new narrative sections.

verses.english_text: When no bush of the field was yet in the land and no small plant of the field had yet sprung up — for the LORD God had not yet caused it to rain on the land, and there was no man to work the ground —
verses.literal_text: And-any shrub-of the-field was-not yet in-the-land and-any plant-of the-field not-yet grew, for the-LORD God had-not rained upon the-land and-man was-not to-work the-ground.
verses.original_text: וְכֹל שִׂיחַ הַשָּׂדֶה טֶרֶם יִהְיֶה בָאָרֶץ וְכָל עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה טֶרֶם יִצְמָח כִּי לֹא הִמְטִיר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים עַל הָאָרֶץ וְאָדָם אַיִן לַעֲבֹד אֶת הָאֲדָמָה׃
verses.transliteration: Vechol siach hasadeh terem yihyeh ba'arets vechol esev hasadeh terem yitsmach ki lo himtir YHWH Elohim al ha'arets ve'adam ayin la'avod et ha'adama.

verses.english_text: And a mist was going up from the land and was watering the whole face of the ground —
verses.literal_text: And-a-mist would-go-up from the-land and-would-water all face-of the-ground —
verses.original_text: וְאֵד יַעֲלֶה מִן הָאָרֶץ וְהִשְׁקָה אֶת כָּל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה׃
verses.transliteration: Ve'ed ya'aleh min ha'arets vehishka et kol peney ha'adama.

verses.english_text: then the LORD God formed the man of dust from the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living creature.
verses.literal_text: And-formed the-LORD God the-man dust from-the-ground and-breathed in-his-nostrils breath-of life, and-became the-man for-living soul.
verses.original_text: וַיִּיצֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם עָפָר מִן הָאֲדָמָה וַיִּפַּח בְּאַפָּיו נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים וַיְהִי הָאָדָם לְנֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה׃
verses.transliteration: Vayitser YHWH Elohim et ha'adam afar min ha'adama vayipach be'apav nishmat chayyim vayehi ha'adam lenefesh chaya.
verses.verse_note: God formed (yatsar — like a potter) and breathed directly into man. No other creature receives this personal divine breath.
verses.language_note: Adam connects with adamah (ground) — emphasising both earthly origin and dignity as image-bearer.

verses.english_text: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, and there He put the man whom He had formed.
verses.literal_text: And-planted the-LORD God garden in-Eden from-east, and-set there the-man whom he-had-formed.
verses.original_text: וַיִּטַּע יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים גַּן בְּעֵדֶן מִקֶּדֶם וַיָּשֶׂם שָׁם אֶת הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר יָצָר׃
verses.transliteration: Vayita YHWH Elohim gan be'Eden mikedem vayasem sham et ha'adam asher yatsar.
verses.historical_note: The location in Eden, in the east likely refers to ancient Mesopotamia near the Tigris and Euphrates.

verses.english_text: And out of the ground the LORD God made to spring up every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food. The tree of life was in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
verses.literal_text: And-caused-to-grow the-LORD God from the-ground every tree desired for-sight and-good for-food, and-the-tree-of life in-midst-of the-garden and-the-tree-of knowledge-of good-and-evil.
verses.original_text: וַיַּצְמַח יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים מִן הָאֲדָמָה כָּל עֵץ נֶחְמָד לְמַרְאֶה וְטוֹב לְמַאֲכָל וְעֵץ הַחַיִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן וְעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע׃
verses.transliteration: Vayatsmach YHWH Elohim min ha'adama kol ets nechmad lemar'eh vetov lema'achal ve'ets hachayim betoch hagan ve'ets hada'at tov vara.

verses.english_text: A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and there it divided and became four rivers.
verses.literal_text: And-a-river going out from-Eden to-water the-garden; and from-there it-separated and-became four heads.
verses.original_text: וְנָהָר יֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן וּמִשָּׁם יִפָּרֵד וְהָיָה לְאַרְבָּעָה רָאשִׁים׃
verses.transliteration: Venahar yotse me'Eden lehashkot et hagan umisham yipared vehaya le'arba'ah rashim.
verses.historical_note: The four rivers ground the garden narrative geographically in the ancient Near East.

verses.english_text: The name of the first is the Pishon. It is the one that flowed around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
verses.literal_text: The name-of the-first Pishon: it the-one flowing around all land-of Havilah, where there the-gold.
verses.original_text: שֵׁם הָאֶחָד פִּישׁוֹן הוּא הַסֹּבֵב אֵת כָּל אֶרֶץ הַחֲוִילָה אֲשֶׁר שָׁם הַזָּהָב׃
verses.transliteration: Shem ha'echad pishon hu hasovev et kol erets haChavila asher sham hazahav.

verses.english_text: And the gold of that land is good; bdellium and onyx stone are there.
verses.literal_text: And the-gold of that land good; there the-bdellium and the-onyx stone.
verses.original_text: וּזֲהַב הָאָרֶץ הַהִוא טוֹב שָׁם הַבְּדֹלַח וְאֶבֶן הַשֹּׁהַם׃
verses.transliteration: Uzahav ha'arets hahi'a tov sham habedolach ve'even hashoham.

verses.english_text: The name of the second river is the Gihon. It is the one that flowed around the whole land of Cush.
verses.literal_text: And name-of the-second river Gihon: it the-one flowing-around all land-of Cush.
verses.original_text: וְשֵׁם הַנָּהָר הַשֵּׁנִי גִּיחוֹן הוּא הַסּוֹבֵב אֵת כָּל אֶרֶץ כּוּשׁ׃
verses.transliteration: Veshem hanahar hasheni Gichon hu hasovev et kol erets Kush.

verses.english_text: And the name of the third river is the Tigris, which flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
verses.literal_text: And name-of the-third river Tigris: it the-one going east-of Assyria. And the-fourth river is the Euphrates.
verses.original_text: וְשֵׁם הַנָּהָר הַשְּׁלִישִׁי חִדֶּקֶל הוּא הַהֹלֵךְ קִדְמַת אַשּׁוּר וְהַנָּהָר הָרְבִיעִי הוּא פְרָת׃
verses.transliteration: Veshem hanahar hashelishi Chidekel hu haholech kidmat Ashur vehanahar harevi'i hu Ferat.
verses.historical_note: The Tigris and Euphrates still flow today, confirming the Mesopotamian setting of the Eden narrative.

verses.english_text: The LORD God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to work it and keep it.
verses.literal_text: And-took the-LORD God the-man and-put-him in-garden-of Eden to-work-it and-to-keep-it.
verses.original_text: וַיִּקַּח יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם וַיַּנִּחֵהוּ בְגַן עֵדֶן לְעָבְדָהּ וּלְשָׁמְרָהּ׃
verses.transliteration: Vayikach YHWH Elohim et ha'adam vayanichehu vegan Eden le'avdah uleshomrah.
verses.verse_note: The verbs work (abad) and keep (shamar) are the same used for priestly tabernacle service — the garden is a sacred space.
verses.cultural_note: Humanity's vocation is stewardship: care, protection, and accountability — not exploitation.

verses.english_text: And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, "You may surely eat of every tree of the garden,"
verses.literal_text: And-commanded the-LORD God upon the-man saying, From-every tree-of the-garden eating you-may-eat,
verses.original_text: וַיְצַו יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים עַל הָאָדָם לֵאמֹר מִכֹּל עֵץ הַגָּן אָכֹל תֹּאכֵל׃
verses.transliteration: Vaytsav YHWH Elohim al ha'adam lemor mikol ets hagan achol tochel.

verses.english_text: "but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat, for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die."
verses.literal_text: But-from tree-of knowledge-of good-and-evil, you-shall-not eat from-it; for in-the-day-of your-eating from-it dying you-shall-die.
verses.original_text: וּמֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע לֹא תֹאכַל מִמֶּנּוּ כִּי בְּיוֹם אֲכָלְךָ מִמֶּנּוּ מוֹת תָּמוּת׃
verses.transliteration: Ume'ets hada'at tov vara lo tochel mimenu ki beyom achalecha mimenu mot tamut.
verses.verse_note: The first divine prohibition. The double form mot tamut (dying you shall die) is emphatic — stressing certainty of death.

verses.english_text: Then the LORD God said, "It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper fit for him."
verses.literal_text: And-said the-LORD God, Not good-is the-being-of the-man by-himself; I-will-make for-him a-help corresponding-to-him.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים לֹא טוֹב הֱיוֹת הָאָדָם לְבַדּוֹ אֶעֱשֶׂה לּוֹ עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer YHWH Elohim lo tov heyot ha'adam levado e'eseh lo ezer kenegdo.
verses.verse_note: The first not good in Scripture in a context of perfect creation — relationship, not solitude, is the design.
verses.language_note: Ezer kenegdo: helper corresponding to him. Ezer is used of God as Israel's helper in 16 Psalms — a position of strength.

verses.english_text: Now out of the ground the LORD God had formed every beast of the field and every bird of the heavens and brought them to the man to see what he would call them. And whatever the man called every living creature, that was its name.
verses.literal_text: And-formed the-LORD God from-the-ground every beast-of the-field and-every bird-of the-heavens, and-brought to the-man to-see what he-would-call-it; and-whatever the-man called it living-soul, that its-name.
verses.original_text: וַיִּצֶר יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים מִן הָאֲדָמָה כָּל חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה וְאֵת כָּל עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וַיָּבֵא אֶל הָאָדָם לִרְאוֹת מַה יִּקְרָא לוֹ וְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָא לוֹ הָאָדָם נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה הוּא שְׁמוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: Vayitser YHWH Elohim min ha'adama kol chayyat hasadeh ve'et kol of hashamayim vayave el ha'adam lir'ot mah yikra lo vechol asher yikra lo ha'adam nefesh chaya hu shemo.
verses.verse_note: Adam naming the animals demonstrates vice-regency over creation — naming confers authority in the ancient Near East.

verses.english_text: The man gave names to all livestock and to the birds of the heavens and to every beast of the field. But for Adam there was not found a helper fit for him.
verses.literal_text: And-the-man called names to-all the-livestock and-to-birds-of the-heavens and-to-every beast-of the-field; but-for-Adam not-found helper corresponding-to-him.
verses.original_text: וַיִּקְרָא הָאָדָם שֵׁמוֹת לְכָל הַבְּהֵמָה וּלְעוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם וּלְכֹל חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה וּלְאָדָם לֹא מָצָא עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ׃
verses.transliteration: Vayikra ha'adam shemot lechol habehema ule'of hashamayim ulechol chayyat hasadeh ule'adam lo matsa ezer kenegdo.
verses.verse_note: No animal was a suitable partner — emphasising the uniqueness of human personhood and necessity of human-to-human communion.

verses.english_text: So the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and while he slept took one of his ribs and closed up its place with flesh.
verses.literal_text: And-caused-to-fall the-LORD God a-deep-sleep upon the-man, and-he-slept; and-took one-of his-ribs and-closed flesh under-it.
verses.original_text: וַיַּפֵּל יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים תַּרְדֵּמָה עַל הָאָדָם וַיִּישָׁן וַיִּקַּח אַחַת מִצַּלְעֹתָיו וַיִּסְגֹּר בָּשָׂר תַּחְתֶּנָּה׃
verses.transliteration: Vayapel YHWH Elohim tardemah al ha'adam vayishan vayikach achat mitsalotav vayisgor basar tachtenah.
verses.language_note: Tsela (rib) can also mean side — the woman may be formed from the man's entire side, one flesh from the beginning.

verses.english_text: And the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man He made into a woman and brought her to the man.
verses.literal_text: And-built the-LORD God the-rib which he-took from the-man into-a-woman and-brought-her to the-man.
verses.original_text: וַיִּבֶן יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶת הַצֵּלָע אֲשֶׁר לָקַח מִן הָאָדָם לְאִשָּׁה וַיְבִאֶהָ אֶל הָאָדָם׃
verses.transliteration: Vayiven YHWH Elohim et hatsela asher lakach min ha'adam le'ishah vayevi'eha el ha'adam.

verses.english_text: Then the man said, "This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man."
verses.literal_text: And-said the-man, This-time bone from-my-bones and-flesh from-my-flesh; this shall-be-called Woman, because from-man this-one was-taken.
verses.original_text: וַיֹּאמֶר הָאָדָם זֹאת הַפַּעַם עֶצֶם מֵעֲצָמַי וּבָשָׂר מִבְּשָׂרִי לְזֹאת יִקָּרֵא אִשָּׁה כִּי מֵאִישׁ לֻקֳחָה זֹּאת׃
verses.transliteration: Vayomer ha'adam zot hapa'am etsem me'atsamai uvasar mivsari lezot yikare ishah ki me'ish lukechah zot.
verses.verse_note: The man's first recorded speech — joyful recognition of likeness and difference.
verses.language_note: Ish/ishah wordplay: man/woman. This at last (zot hapa'am) expresses joy after no animal was a suitable partner.

verses.english_text: Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.
verses.literal_text: Therefore shall-leave a-man his-father and-his-mother and-shall-cling to-his-wife; and-they-shall-be for-one flesh.
verses.original_text: עַל כֵּן יַעֲזָב אִישׁ אֶת אָבִיו וְאֶת אִמּוֹ וְדָבַק בְּאִשְׁתּוֹ וְהָיוּ לְבָשָׂר אֶחָד׃
verses.transliteration: Al ken ya'azov ish et aviv ve'et imo vedavak be'ishto vehayu levasar echad.
verses.verse_note: Marriage as a creation ordinance — a re-union of what was originally one. Jesus quotes this in Matthew 19:5.

verses.english_text: And the man and his wife were both naked and were not ashamed.
verses.literal_text: And-were-both-of-them the-man and-his-wife naked and-were-not ashamed.
verses.original_text: וַיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם עֲרוּמִּים הָאָדָם וְאִשְׁתּוֹ וְלֹא יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ׃
verses.transliteration: Vayihyu shneihem arumim ha'adam ve'ishto velo yitboshashu.
verses.verse_note: Nakedness without shame signals perfect integrity — full transparency before God and each other.
verses.language_note: Arumim (naked) creates a wordplay with arum (crafty) in Genesis 3:1 — setting up narrative tension.

root_words.core_conceptual_meaning: To create, to bring into existence — used exclusively of divine activity
root_words.extended_meaning: Unlike asah (make), bara never has a human subject. It always describes creation that originates with God, often implying absolute origination.
root_words.usage_evolution: Throughout the OT, bara consistently refers to divine creative acts. It is never trivial or mundane.

root_words.core_conceptual_meaning: Head, beginning, first, top — that which comes first

root_words.extended_meaning: Elohim is plural in form but used with singular verbs for Israel's God, expressing fullness and majesty of divine power.

root_words.core_conceptual_meaning: To cease, to rest, to stop — root of the Sabbath concept
root_words.extended_meaning: From the physical act of stopping work, shavat evolved into the theological concept of sacred rest patterned on God's own cessation.
root_words.usage_evolution: The Sabbath concept moves from cessation of physical work to eschatological rest (Hebrews 4).

root_words.core_conceptual_meaning: To form, to shape — used of a potter working clay
root_words.usage_evolution: Used throughout OT for God as divine potter forming creation, humanity, and Israel (Isa 45:9, Jer 18:6).

root_words.core_conceptual_meaning: To help, to aid, to support — a position of strength
root_words.usage_evolution: Used 21 times in OT. 16 occurrences refer to God himself as Israel's helper in the Psalms — not an inferior role.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Beginning, first, chief, firstfruits. The absolute first of anything — temporal, positional, or qualitative.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Reshit comes from rosh (head) and carries the idea of that which comes first in a series. As a construct noun in Gen 1:1 it means in the beginning of, pointing to the initiation of all created reality.
lexical_entries.usage_notes: Also used for the firstfruits of harvest (Deut 26:2) and for wisdom as the beginning (Prov 4:7).
lexical_entries.cultural_background: Ancient Near Eastern creation texts also begin with temporal clauses, but none use this exact formula.
lexical_entries.translation_alternatives: ["In the beginning","At the start","When God began to create"]
lexical_entries.theological_significance: The first word of the Hebrew Bible establishes time itself as a created category — God precedes the beginning.

lexical_entries.part_of_speech: Verb, Qal, perfect, 3rd person, masculine, singular
lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: To create, to shape, to bring forth. Used exclusively with God as subject.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Bara appears 48 times in the OT. It is never used with a human subject — always God who bara. While it does not in itself demand creation from nothing (ex nihilo), the context of Gen 1:1 implies absolute origination.
lexical_entries.usage_notes: Compare with asah (make, H6213) which is more generic. Bara is reserved for acts uniquely possible for God.
lexical_entries.cultural_background: In Mesopotamian creation texts, gods shape pre-existing material. Hebrew bara implies a qualitatively different kind of creation.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: The exclusive divine usage of bara establishes a Creator-creature distinction fundamental to the entire biblical worldview.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: God, gods, divine beings. The plural of El/Eloah, used most frequently for the God of Israel.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Elohim is the most common Hebrew word for God (2,570 occurrences). Its plural form expresses the fullness and completeness of divine power. When used of Israel's God it consistently takes singular verbs.
lexical_entries.usage_notes: Used for the God of Israel (singular meaning, plural form), for pagan gods (plural), and for divine beings in some contexts.
lexical_entries.cultural_background: Ancient Canaanite religion had El as a high god and Elim for a divine council. Hebrew Bible radically redefines this vocabulary.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: The use of Elohim in the creation narrative is universal and cosmic — not a tribal deity but the creator of all things.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Heavens, sky. The Hebrew word is always plural in form.
Earth, land, ground, territory. Context determines whether the reference is to the whole earth or a particular land.
Formlessness, wasteland, emptiness, unreality, chaos.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Tohu describes utter formlessness and desolation. In Gen 1:2 it pairs with bohu in the formula tohu va-bohu. The phrase became an idiom for utter desolation (Isa 34:11, Jer 4:23).
lexical_entries.cultural_background: Tohu connects to the Akkadian concept of primordial chaos. Genesis radically reorients it around a sovereign, personal God.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Void, emptiness. Only ever appears alongside tohu.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Bohu occurs only 3 times in the OT, always paired with tohu. Its etymology is uncertain. The alliterative pairing became the biblical shorthand for primordial nothingness.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Spirit, wind, breath. The word covers the full range from physical wind to the divine Spirit.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Ruach is one of the most theologically rich words in the OT. In Gen 1:2 it refers to the active, creative presence of God hovering over the formless deep — signalling God's engagement with and authority over creation.
lexical_entries.cultural_background: In Mesopotamian texts, wind was a divine force but not a personal presence. Here ruach Elohim is the personal active energy of the creator God.
lexical_entries.translation_alternatives: ["Spirit of God","wind of God","mighty wind","breath of God"]
lexical_entries.theological_significance: The Spirit's presence over the waters anticipates his role in new creation (John 3:5-8) and the renewal of all things.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Light, daylight, sunlight, lightning.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: In Gen 1:3, or is the first created thing, preceding the sun and moon. This theological ordering reflects the Hebrew understanding that light is not dependent on the sun — it is its own created reality.
lexical_entries.cultural_background: In Egyptian cosmology, the sun-god Ra was central. By placing light before the luminaries, Genesis implicitly subordinates them to God's word.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: The association of light with God's presence becomes a major biblical theme (John 1:4-5, 1 John 1:5).

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Definite direct object marker — has no English equivalent.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: The particle et marks a definite direct object in Hebrew. It is untranslatable in English. Its presence signals that what follows is a specific, definite object. Its first occurrence in Gen 1:1 marking the heavens and earth has generated rich theological discussion.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: Some rabbinic commentators assigned mystical significance to the aleph-tav combination, seeing it as encompassing all of Hebrew letters — suggesting creation encompasses everything from aleph to tav.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: To be, to become, to exist, to happen.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Hayah is the primary Hebrew verb of existence. In Gen 1:2 it describes the state of the earth (was formless). In the wayyiqtol form it narrates historical sequence. The divine name YHWH is derived from this root — the One who is/was/will be.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: The name YHWH (LORD) derives from hayah — the self-existent, eternal One (Exod 3:14).

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: To say, to speak, to declare, to command.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: In Genesis 1, amar appears 10 times — consistently as the vehicle of God's creative activity. The formula vayomer Elohim (and God said) introduces each creative command, establishing that God creates by speaking — an idea John picks up in identifying Jesus as the Logos (Word) in John 1.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: Divine speech as the mechanism of creation anticipates the New Testament identification of Jesus as the creative Word (John 1:1-3).

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: To make, to do, to produce, to accomplish.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Asah is more generic than bara. While bara is used exclusively of God, asah can be used of both human and divine activity. In Genesis 1, both verbs appear — bara for the initial creative act and asah for the fashioning of specific elements.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Man, mankind, human being, humanity.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Adam is both the generic word for humanity and the name of the first man. It connects etymologically with adamah (ground/earth) — humans are earthly beings who bear the divine image. This paradox of dust and dignity is central to biblical anthropology.
lexical_entries.cultural_background: The connection between humans and earth (adamah/adam) was common in ancient Near Eastern thought. Genesis gives it a unique theological dimension — humans are both dust and image-bearers.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: Adam as image-bearer (tselem Elohim) establishes the basis of human dignity, value, and responsibility before God.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Image, likeness, resemblance, representation.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: In the ancient Near East, tselem was used for royal statues that represented the king in territories where he could not personally be present. In Genesis 1:26-27, this concept is radically democratised — every human being, not just the king, bears the image of the divine ruler.
lexical_entries.cultural_background: ANE kings erected tselem statues to assert dominion over distant regions. Genesis transfers this concept from kings to all humanity.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: The imago Dei (image of God) is foundational to human dignity, creativity, morality, and responsibility. It is the basis for the prohibition of murder (Gen 9:6) and the Great Commandment.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: To form, to fashion, to shape — used of a potter working clay, and of God forming living creatures.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Yatsar implies careful, intentional craftsmanship. Its use in Gen 2:7 (formed the man from dust) emphasises the personal, hands-on nature of God's creative work with humanity, contrasting with the cosmic scale of Gen 1.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Dust, earth, dry loose earth, ash, powder.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Afar emphasises the basic material nature of humanity — taken from the ground and returning to it (Gen 3:19). Its use in Gen 2:7 balances the dignity of the image of God with the humility of creaturely dependence.
lexical_entries.cultural_background: In ancient Near Eastern literature, humans were often made from clay or mixed materials. Hebrew afar (dust) emphasises even greater frailty and dependence on God.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: You are dust and to dust you shall return (Gen 3:19) — the mortality of humanity is grounded in the raw material of its creation.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Breath, breath of life, soul, spirit — the life-giving breath from God.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Neshamah is the divine breath that animates human life. In Gen 2:7, God breathes it directly into man's nostrils — an intimate personal act unparalleled in the creation of any other creature. This direct impartation distinguishes human life as uniquely sacred.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: The neshamah is what makes humans nefesh chaya (living beings). It is the source of human consciousness, moral sensitivity, and relationship with God.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Sabbath, rest, cessation. The seventh day of the week set apart for rest and worship.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Shabbat derives from the verb shavat (to cease). The Sabbath is first instituted not by commandment but by God's own example in Genesis 2. It becomes the sign of the Mosaic covenant (Exod 31:13) and points toward ultimate eschatological rest.
lexical_entries.cultural_background: The concept of a seventh-day rest was unique in the ancient Near East. No neighbouring culture had a regular weekly rest day.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: The Sabbath is woven into the fabric of creation itself. Jesus describes himself as Lord of the Sabbath (Matt 12:8), and Hebrews 4 uses it as a picture of the eternal rest available in Christ.

lexical_entries.lexical_meaning: Helper, aid, support. One who provides essential assistance.
lexical_entries.extended_definition: Ezer occurs 21 times in the OT. In 16 of those occurrences it refers to God himself as the helper of Israel (Pss 121:2; 124:8). The use for the woman in Gen 2:18 places her in the company of God as one who provides indispensable help — not a subordinate role but a necessary, powerful one.
lexical_entries.theological_significance: The woman as ezer parallels God as Israel's ezer — a source of strength and rescue, not mere assistance.
